audit.title: Glossary (DTA Technical Standard)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; each term opens with its definition ("A security mechanism used throughout the DTA technical standard to grant explicit permission…"). No back-references. Ideal glossary chunking.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 21 headings, 1 H1, no level skips, median 31 words per section — each entry is a clean retrievable unit. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak; only 2 numerals in 788 words, vague quantifiers "many, some". Even NAV TTL, which is inherently numeric, could name concrete example windows. Glossaries can still cite parameter units and limits.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak; only 2 internal links, 0 external/primary. Terms like "CCIP" and "Chain Selector" should link to their canonical spec/reference pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong; this is the page's purpose and it delivers verbatim-liftable definitions (e.g. NAV: "The price per share of a fund.").

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Very weak; no JSON-LD (`DefinedTermSet`/`DefinedTerm` would be ideal here), no canonical, no visible dates. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable to a glossary; scored neutral, no deduction intended.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good for definitional "what is X" intent; lacks symptom/error-phrased entries, but that is out of scope for a glossary.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong prose, but **Fund Administrator** and **Transfer Agent** carry *word-for-word identical* definitions, which harms entity resolution — an engine cannot distinguish the two roles.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured glossary: 21 term entries, each a self-contained H2 section with a crisp one-to-two-sentence definition — an inherently extractable format that maps directly to "what is X" queries. Its biggest GEO weakness is the complete absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dateModified) combined with near-zero linking to primary sources and thin quantitative specifics. The honest verdict: strong bones for a glossary, but it under-earns on discoverability signals and cross-references that would let engines cite it confidently over sibling pages.

recommendations.title: Add `DefinedTermSet` / `DefinedTerm` JSON-LD
recommendations.change: Emit a `DefinedTermSet` with each H2 as a `DefinedTerm` (name + description), plus a canonical URL and `dateModified`. This is the schema type engines expect for glossaries.
recommendations.why: Structured term schema plus freshness/canonical signals raise parse-ability and citation trust (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Disambiguate Fund Administrator vs Transfer Agent
recommendations.where: the two entries, currently identical text
recommendations.issue: both read "responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of a fund…"
recommendations.change: Rewrite one to state the distinguishing responsibility and lead with the difference (e.g. Transfer Agent's role in the shareholder register / legal record vs Administrator's operational tasks).
recommendations.why: Identical definitions cause entity collisions; engines may conflate or cite the wrong role.

recommendations.title: Link key terms to their canonical reference pages
recommendations.where: Chain Selector, CCIP, Onchain Settlement (Cross-Chain), Primary Chain
recommendations.issue: "0 external, 0 to primary sources"; only CCIP links out.
recommendations.change: Add inline links from Chain Selector and cross-chain terms to the CCIP reference / chain-selector docs; link NAV TTL to its parameter reference.
recommendations.why: Attributable, cross-referenced definitions raise citation rate and let engines assemble justified multi-hop answers.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics where the concept is quantitative
recommendations.change: For NAV TTL give a concrete example ("e.g. `3600` = 1-hour window"); the Request Lifecycle already lists states verbatim — keep that pattern and note any timeout semantics.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics with units are among the highest-lift changes for extraction.

recommendations.title: Surface a visible last-updated line
recommendations.where: top of page under the intro
recommendations.change: Add a rendered "Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD" plus the `dateModified` in schema.
recommendations.why: Visible freshness is an independent trust signal for engines skimming the page.

antiPatterns: **Duplicate definitions** — Fund Administrator and Transfer Agent are textually identical (entity-resolution hazard).
**Vague quantifiers** — "many, some" flagged; minor for a glossary but avoidable.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references, no undated wall-of-text issues.
offPageNotes: Page already references `/llms.txt` — good; ensure this glossary URL is actually enumerated there.
Canonical URL, sitemap inclusion, and site-level `TechArticle`/`DefinedTermSet` templating are site-level; fix once in the docs framework to benefit all reference pages.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content — pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a complete metadata read.
